newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - DEC 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - DEC 2.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:
--Face-off between government and farmers as farmers declare they are ready to spend Christmas on the roads and the weekend's bad weather fails to move them, as hoped by the government.

--The Xanthi prefecture bears the brunt of the country's weekend torrential rainfall. Three drowned, dozens were left homeless and cars were swallowed up in raging waters as the Kosinthos river broke its banks.
--Merchants on Athens, Thessaloniki and other major shopping thoroughfares will pay between 20-43 percent more taxes under new adjusted objective tax criteria.
--Meteorologists forecast more storms to come with relief from heavy rain and strong winds in sight on Thursday.

--Those liable for the government's new real estate tax will pay over three bimonthly instalments, Deputy Finance Minister George Drys says. The tax will be imposed on persons and companies with real estate valued at over 60 million drachmas.
--Agriculture Minister Stephanos Tzoumakas says the farmers' protests are justified and that Greece must work towards a better status for its products at the European Union.

--Thessaloniki feels the effects of the blockade of national roads over the weekend while the effects begin to be felt in Athens. Milk supplies are expected to be the first products hit by the 27 blockades on national roads.
--Secondary school teachers shut down state schools for three days next week in an attempt to get the ministry to withdraw the new wage scale.
--The Xanthi storm swept buildings, bridges and roads in its wake. Thousands of hectares of farm land have been flooded. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
